text: One of the biggest sites dedicated to video game decompilations is sunsetting due to the growth of AI. In recent years, fan developers have been taking on a number of ‘decompilation’ projects, in which they take an existing game and reverse-engineer it into readable code. These decompilations – which are technically legal because the developers do not use any leaked content or copyrighted assets, and require players to provide their own legally-sourced ROMs – open up the ability to improve games further with support for higher frame rates, widescreen and ultrawide aspect ratios, dual-stick controls and other user-made mods. The growth of AI has led to issues, however, with the community divided on whether using AI for these projects is a positive step (because it makes it much quicker) or a negative one. Now the website Decomp.dev , which indexes decompilations and tracks those projects currently in progress, will be ‘sunsetting’, as announced by its creator @encounter. In a statement posted on the site’s homepage, @encounter notes that while they don’t believe AI is the main issue in itself, because when used properly and ethically it “can expedite the decompilation process in a significant way”, the “community aspect of decompilation has been broken” by people using AI in more questionable ways. “Our projects have always been open source to encourage contributions and to benefit the community as a whole,” they wrote. “Bad actors have been abusing this in increasingly troublesome ways.” @example explained that some people have been taking existing decompilation projects which are currently in progress, forking them and “finishing” them with AI.
